DESIGN PROTOTYPE
Technical design / Entity relocation · edition 08

Bring the legal entity home.

Add Mumbai as a fourth physical store, move the India entity while source operations continue, then change authority once and account for old copies.

Executable relocation workspace

Open the animated migration monitor →. Hosted mode is a browser simulation. The unified development lab requires four CockroachDB containers and regional OPA. Earlier SQLite results are historical adapter tests, not deployment evidence. The existing 30-entity catalog and normalized business examples remain separate.

A lawful transition, explicitly modeled

This isolated LE-IN-01 fixture permits Singapore before simulated t=600 and requires India afterwards. The clock advances only through the deadline control. It is a hypothetical policy change, not a statement of Indian law. The original India-only catalog example continues to reject Singapore. Registration creates a staging destination; it does not grant permission to serve or export data.

Identity / authorityBefore migrationAfter activation
Legal entityLE-IN-01LE-IN-01, unchanged
Physical homeSG / SingaporeIN / Mumbai
Writer authorityEpoch 1Epoch 2; SG durably fenced
Placement directoryVersion 1Version 2, ACTIVE only after target enable
Business keysP-001, R-001, H-001, GLOBAL-001Same keys and owner; no geographic re-keying
US payloadZeroZero

How business services use the new store

Provision the India cell with its local database, business services, OPA, gateway, message transport, keys, observability and backup policies. The business gateway resolves legal entity to home and placement epoch, then routes privately to the regional service. Services recheck authority in their local transactions; gateway caches cannot authorize a stale writer. Retry a stale route only with a refreshed directory and the original idempotency key.

The proof of concept represents these interfaces in one FastAPI process. It uses four independent CockroachDB single-node containers in the unified Compose deployment. All local geographies are logical labels. This is not local HA or physical residency evidence.

The movement and authority sequence

01Prepare

Register India; verify entity, country, table and key restrictions; retain capture history.

02Copy + catch up

Capture snapshot and sequence; copy bounded batches while source writes append changes.

03Validate

Reconcile contents, row versions, tombstones, applied sequence and graph closure.

04Fence + activate

Durably stop the SG writer; final drain; persist IN route as ACTIVATING; enable epoch 2; mark ACTIVE.

05Dispose

Bounded old live-row cleanup; separately account for history, backups and audit obligations.

State / failureRequired outcome
Source write after validationInvalidate validation and return to catch-up.
Destination paused during copyNo transfer; lawful source operations continue.
Crash after source fenceDetect durable fence on restart; remain unavailable until recovery.
Crash after IN route checkpointACTIVATING blocks commands until target enable is safely resumed.
Old source route or transfer envelopeReject stale authority/epoch, even after the gateway cache expires.
Deadline missedFail closed for affected SG reads/writes/export; show residual copies.
Attempted reverse routing after target writesReject. Recover forward or perform a new lawful reverse migration.

Transaction boundaries and operational priority

Local transactionContentsOutside the transaction
Source business commandAuthority/epoch check + changed rows + versions + local journal + request receiptCopy, cross-region policy decisions and remote acknowledgements
SnapshotConsistent entity rows and source sequenceBounded destination apply and cursor advancement
Target batchStaging authority check + versioned row/tombstone applyCheckpoint update; retry may repeat the batch
Source fenceWritable=false + final source sequenceDestination verification and route activation
Activation sagaPersist ACTIVATING route, then target writable epoch, then ACTIVENo cross-store atomic transaction; crash can pause availability
CleanupBounded source live deletes; final fixture journal/receipt/snapshot purgeWAL/MVCC/backups/archive disposal evidence

The PoC keeps its routing/job row in SG after business cutover, so SG remains a controller availability dependency; retiring that whole cell is not demonstrated. A pilot needs a resilient, appropriately located directory and regional authority state. One entity lock makes the small slice deterministic. An unrelated UK command uses a different lock and store; tests prove it can commit while the India lock is held. This does not prove distributed or performance isolation. The pilot must separate guard, operational and migration queues, relays, worker groups, connection budgets, retry paths and I/O admission. Migration takes capped bulk capacity and yields when measured foreground p99 or lock pressure breaches its budget.

The fixture scans at most 193 envelopes. At 100M relationships, replace snapshot materialization and final comparison with consistent range scans, per-shard capture/application checkpoints and partitioned manifests. Existing latency targets remain pilot hypotheses. Start with no more than 10% foreground p99 degradation against the same hardware and offered workload without migration; measure errors, tail latency and catch-up lag. Establish an explicit entity cutover-pause budget from measurements.

Operational model adapter: what moves

Business scopeIncluded in this slicePilot extension
Party and ownershipEntity-private party plus global_party_id; relationship and party_relationshipMove private owner data; reauthorize minimal global identity separately
Product and servicingHolding, contact, consent, preference, historyMaintain table/key/purpose constraints and aggregate visibility
Alternate identifiersParty, relationship and holding IDsPreserve owner-qualified keys and reference closure
Classification and sovereigntyClassification row plus parallel policy envelopeVersioned rule/fact/grant/placement metadata; deny precedence
Federation recipientsNo recipient grants in the migration fixtureHandoff pending outbound intents and inbound projections without inventing entitlements

The executable adapter uses typed envelopes in mig_rows and validates parents before activation. It does not yet move the existing normalized business.* tables. Staging remains inaccessible to ordinary reads. A normalized adapter must load parents safely, enforce foreign keys, expose complete aggregates and preserve idempotency receipts. Moving one entity must not move another entity’s relationships or make all contact data global.

OPA policy and API outline

API / Rego input · design skeleton
POST /v1/data/bank/migration/allow
{"input":{"operation":"transfer","country":"IN","elapsed":0,
  "deadline":600,"conflict":false,"home":"SG","target":"IN","phase":"COPYING"}}

GET  /api/migration
POST /api/migration/register | plan | start
POST /api/migration/copy | catchup       {"batch":8}
POST /api/migration/validate | fence | activate | cleanup
POST /api/migration/write               {"kind":"update","request_id":"unique","expected_epoch":1}
GET  /api/migration/read/IN
# Synthetic faults: pause, conflict, deadline, stale, rollback.
# Scoped reset: {"scenario":"synthetic-india"}. Conflicts return HTTP 409.
# API outlines above are implemented by the isolated local migration adapter.

Inputs come from trusted coordinator facts. The module defaults deny for other geographies; an India exclusion blocks the transfer. Runtime route, epoch and staging checks complement OPA. Configure separate source and India OPA endpoints for export/import admission. An unavailable decision service fails closed. Signed bundles, authoritative fact freshness, optimistic control revisions, jurisdiction-aware administration and approval roles are pilot work.

Change capture, telemetry and evidence

The slice journals business changes in the same local SQL transaction. Extend this to an operational outbox plus region-local CockroachDB CDC and a durable message bus such as Kafka, with separate guard, operational and bulk lanes. Filter and authorize projections before any cross-border bus. CockroachDB CDC can duplicate messages and does not guarantee whole-transaction delivery order. Source resolved progress is distinct from target applied progress; preserve resource versions, tombstones, manifests and idempotency.

Migration spans carry bounded work.class values. Tests capture real OpenTelemetry spans in memory; the unified Docker acceptance observes Collector spans and trace-correlated Loki application logs. A searchable trace backend remains pilot work. Add per-shard lag, copied bytes, stale-write denials, cutover pause and cleanup-age metrics. Keep customer IDs out of metric labels and payloads out of global traces.

The monitor’s recent events are not immutable audit. Pilot audit uses regional transactional intents and an idempotent append-only relay recording authority changes, actor, policy versions, manifests and disposal evidence. COMPLETE means live fixture cleanup, not erasure from WAL/MVCC, backups, audit archives or caches. Retained surfaces and deadlines need their own evidence and exception workflow.

Verified scope and pilot handoff

Executed: browser state-machine assertions; actual SQLite persistence and restart; source-fence and activation crash-gap tests; HTTP read/write guards; real OPA integration; 24 Rego tests including 12 migration cases; OpenTelemetry span capture. The subsequent unified Docker suite and live Chromium generator/migration walkthrough passed, including restart-persistent authority and source cleanup. See the local run guide and container evidence. WAN throughput, distributed fencing, database crash boundaries, HA and production deletion remain pilot gates.

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Implement StoreRegistry, PlacementDirectory, MigrationPlanner, SnapshotReader, ChangeCapture, TargetImporter, AuthorityFence, CutoverCoordinator and DisposalTracker interfaces behind regional Spring Boot APIs. Use an India transition fixture with four physical stores and stable owner/party/relationship/holding keys. Start from the supplied isolated adapter, then implement normalized-table adapters and outgoing/incoming federation handoff explicitly. Keep business transactions local and bounded. Persist per-shard cursors, retain capture history, compare current policy before export/import, apply versions/tombstones idempotently and verify complete graphs. Source fence must commit before target activation; transfer request receipts and preserve event IDs. Require conditional placement CAS and durable regional epoch enforcement; test two controllers and partial failures. Add OTel work-class spans and regional append-only audit intents. Include paused target, policy conflict, deadline, crash/restart, duplicate delivery, old writer, stale transfer, late source update, cleanup and reverse-migration tests. Do not claim single-node containers establish residency/HA or that SQL deletion erases backups. Keep measured, simulated and proposed behavior explicitly labelled.
